findings.title: Date overrides bypass calendar and booking conflicts
findings.body: When an override exists for the slot's date, checkIfIsAvailable returns true before evaluating busy. An availability override does not make existing calendar events or bookings disappear. For example, a host with a 10:00–12:00 override and an existing 10:00–11:00 booking is now reported as available at 10:00. This affects both fixed hosts and round-robin hosts and exposes conflicting slots for booking. Continue checking busy after validating override availability.

findings.title: Require the entire slot to fit within an override
findings.body: The override checks reject slots entirely before the override or starting after its end, but accept slots that only partially overlap it. With a fixed host's 10:00–11:00 override, a 09:30–10:30 or 10:30–11:30 candidate generated from another round-robin host passes this check. A slot starting exactly at 11:00 also passes because isAfter excludes equality. Consequently, the fixed host can still be booked outside their override. Validate that the slot starts at or after the override start and ends at or before its end.

findings.title: Treat multiple override ranges as alternatives
findings.body: dateOverrides.find returns a rejecting range as soon as a slot is outside any override on that date. If a host has overrides of 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, a 10:00 slot is rejected by the afternoon range, while a 14:00 slot is rejected by the morning range. Valid split-day overrides therefore lose their available slots. The check should accept a slot contained in any override range for that date, rather than reject it for being outside another range.

findings.title: Do not reject slots outside a different working-hours range
findings.body: The workingHours.find predicate rejects a slot if it is outside any working-hours range for its weekday. For a normal split schedule of 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, every morning slot is outside the afternoon range and every afternoon slot is outside the morning range, so all valid slots are filtered out. This is a regression for personal events as well as team events because this check now runs for their hosts. Determine whether any applicable range contains the slot instead.

findings.title: Check the slot's actual end against working hours
findings.body: The variable end is calculated from slotStartTime, exactly like start, instead of from slotEndTime. As a result, this check permits an event to extend beyond a host's working-hours end. For example, a fixed host available until 11:00 passes a 10:30–11:30 candidate generated from another host's availability. Compare the actual event end with the working-hours boundary so the entire event fits in the host's schedule.
